[P4] 哈蒂正在房间里做作业，爱德华突然冲了进来。“快，哈蒂，快跟我去看看！”他拽着哈蒂的外套喊着，“我有一个重大发现！”
“这次又是什么啊？”哈蒂一边在计算器上敲着数字，一边有点儿不耐烦地问道。她正在绞尽脑汁做算数题，真没心情去看爱德华的什么“发现”。

[P5] 爱德华等哈蒂不再敲计算器了，才开口小声说道：“我觉得我们花园那头可能住着小小人。”
“爱德华，别犯傻了！”哈蒂说道，“谁都知道世界上没有小小人。你自己去玩吧！”

[P6] 但是，爱德华没动。花园那头就是有小小人，他很确定。于是，他固执地看着哈蒂。
“你看到他们了吗？”哈蒂有点儿恼火了，她想赶紧结束和爱德华的这场胡说八道。
爱德华的脸耷拉了下来，因为他还没亲眼见过小小人，不过他见过他们的东西。“求求你了，哈蒂，跟我去看看嘛！”
哈蒂叹了一口气，说：“好吧，但你得先给我看一些证据。”

[P7] “没问题！”说完，爱德华
就向花园那头走去了。

[P8] 哈蒂算完两道题后，爱德华回来了，手上紧紧攥着什么东西。
“那是什么？”哈蒂问道。爱德华胖乎乎的手指中间露出来一个银白色的东西。
“是我找的证据。”爱德华满脸自豪地说，“是一根超级超级小的拐杖，是小小人用的。”

[P9] 哈蒂瞥了一眼爱德华新找到的宝贝，嘲笑道：“这不是拐杖，就是一根老树枝而已，是从银色的桦树上掉下来的。你得找到比这更有说服力的证据才行！
爱德华皱着眉头，把这根“拐杖”放到了自己的“特别架子”上，然后又消失在了花园里。

[P10] 哈蒂做完三道题之后，爱德华回来了。“哈蒂，看！我找到了一顶超级超级小的帽子。一定是小小人的。”
说着，爱德华张开了小手，露出了一顶造型完美的迷你帽子。
哈蒂可不觉得这有什么：“这不是帽子，只是橡子的盖儿而已！是从橡树上掉下来的。你得找到比这更有说服力的证据！”
爱德华把“帽子”也放在了“特别架子”上，就在微型拐杖旁边，然后又朝花园出发了。

[P11] 这次，哈蒂在爱德华回来之前成功解了四道题。爱德华小心翼翼地抚摸着他找到的宝贝，说：“哈蒂，我这次真的找到了证据。看，是一双超级超级小的毛茸茸的拖鞋！这一定是哪个小小人的。”
“对不起，爱德华，”哈蒂摇着头说，“你找到的根本不是什么毛茸茸的拖鞋，只是柳絮而已，是从褪色柳上掉下来的。你这是在浪费时间。你不可能找到什么证据的，因为世界上根本没有小小人！”

[P12] 爱德华还是不相信。他原本以为毛茸茸的小拖鞋一定可以说服哈蒂的。他把小拖鞋放在了“特别架子”上，就在小帽子和小拐杖旁边。然后，他再一次去了花园。

[P13] 爱德华离开以后，哈蒂观摩了一番爱德华整齐摆放在架子上的那排“宝贝”，她笑了。
“还真相信世界上有小小人呢。”哈蒂这样想着，又回去继续做作业了。

[P14] 爱德华再次信心满满地大步走进房间时，
哈蒂刚好做完最后一道题。
“我找到了！”爱德华兴奋地喊着，“这次我真的找到证据啦。这是一双超级超级小的
翅膀，一定是小小人的！”说着，爱德华把手
上的东西举到了哈蒂眼前。
哈蒂不想继续玩这个游戏了，便说道：“爱
德华，你太傻了。这不是什么神仙翅膀，只是
梧桐树上掉下来的种子。你忘了吗？你以前还
和爷爷一起拿着这个当直升机到处转呢。”
爱德华很伤心。他记得哈蒂说的话。也
许哈蒂是对的，世界上没有独角兽，没有鬼
魂，没有会飞的飞碟，也没有小小人。

[P15] “我已经做完作业了。”哈蒂看着爱德华忧郁的小脸说，“睡觉前，你想不想和我一起踢会儿足球呀？
爱德华脸上又神采飞扬了。他把神仙翅膀放在了架子上，就在小拖鞋、小帽子和小拐杖旁边，然后拿起足球去了花园。最终，他以5:3的比分打败了哈蒂。

[P16] 晚上八点，哈蒂和爱德华上床睡觉了。月光照在他们熟睡的脸上，一阵温柔的轻风从敞着的窗户吹了进来。
在梦里，哈蒂听到爱德华的架子上传来了超级超级小的声音：“我就说花园这头住着超大人嘛！”

[P17] 第二天一早，哈蒂醒来就看到爱德华在兴奋地上蹿下跳。他把哈蒂拉到了特别架子跟前。小拐杖、小帽子、小拖鞋和小翅膀全都不见了。
“看吧，哈蒂！都不见了！小小人把它们都拿走了，这算不算证据？”
“算！”哈蒂倒吸了一口气，“我想可能真的算。”

[P4] Hattie was doing her homework in the room when Edward suddenly burst in. "Hurry, Hattie, come with me quickly!" he shouted, pulling on Hattie's coat. "I have a major discovery!"
"What is it this time?" Hattie asked, tapping numbers on her calculator with a bit of impatience. She was struggling with math problems and really didn't feel like seeing what Edward's "discovery" was.

[P5] Edward waited until Hattie stopped tapping the calculator, then whispered, "I think there might be little people living at the end of our garden." 
"Edward, stop being silly!" Hattie said. "Everyone knows there are no little people. Go play by yourself!"

[P6] But Edward didn't budge. There were little people in the garden, he was sure. So he stubbornly stared at Hattie.
"Did you see them?" Hattie was getting a bit annoyed. She wanted to end this nonsense with Edward quickly.
Edward's face drooped. He hadn't seen the little people himself, but he had seen their things. "Please, Hattie, come and see with me!"
Hattie sighed and said, "Alright, but you have to show me some evidence first."

[P7] "No problem!" said Edward, then he walked towards the other end of the garden.

[P8] After Hattie finished two math problems, Edward came back, tightly holding something in his hand.
"What is that?" Hattie asked. From Edward's chubby fingers, a silvery-white object peeked out.
"It's the evidence I found," Edward said proudly. "It's a super, super tiny cane, for the little people to use."

[P9] Hattie glanced at the new treasure Edward had found and scoffed, "This isn't a cane, it's just an old twig, fallen from a silver birch tree. You need to find more convincing evidence!"
Edward frowned, placed the "cane" on his "special shelf," and then disappeared into the garden again.

[P10] After Hattie finished three math problems, Edward came back. "Hattie, look! I found a super, super tiny hat. It must be a little person's!"
As he spoke, Edward opened his small hand, revealing a perfectly shaped miniature hat.
Hattie didn't think much of it: "That's not a hat, just an acorn cap! It fell off an oak tree. You need to find more convincing evidence!"
Edward put the 'hat' on the 'special shelf', right next to the miniature cane, and then headed back out to the garden.

[P11] This time, Hattie had successfully solved four problems before Edward returned. Edward carefully touched the treasure he had found and said, "Hattie, I've really found evidence this time. Look, it's a pair of super, super tiny, fuzzy slippers! They must belong to some little person." 
"I'm sorry, Edward," Hattie said, shaking her head, "what you found isn't fuzzy slippers at all—it's just willow fluff, fallen from a faded willow tree. You're wasting your time. You can't find any evidence, because little people simply don't exist!"

[P12] Edward still didn't believe. He had thought the fuzzy little slippers would surely convince Hattie. He placed the slippers on the 'special shelf,' right next to the little hat and the tiny cane. Then, he went back to the garden once more.

[P13] After Edward left, Hattie took a look at the row of 'treasures' Edward had neatly arranged on the shelf. She smiled.
"Still believes in little people, does she?" Hattie thought, then went back to her homework.

[P14] When Edward confidently strode back into the room, 
Hattie had just finished her last problem.
"I found it!" Edward exclaimed excitedly, "This time I've really found proof. These are super, super tiny wings—definitely from a little person!" He held up the object in his hand to Hattie's eyes.
Hattie didn't want to play this game anymore. She said, "Edward, you're so silly. These aren't fairy wings at all—they're just seeds that fell from a sycamore tree. Don't you remember? You used to play with these like helicopters with Grandpa." 
Edward was very sad. He remembered what Hattie had said. Maybe Hattie was right—there were no unicorns, no ghosts, no flying saucers, and no little people in the world.

[P15] "I've finished my homework," Hattie said, looking at Edward's gloomy little face. "Before bed, do you want to play a game of soccer with me?"
Edward's face lit up again. He put the fairy wings on the shelf, right next to the little slippers, hat, and cane, then picked up the soccer ball and went to the garden. In the end, he beat Hattie 5 to 3.

[P16] It was eight o'clock at night. Hattie and Edward went to bed. Moonlight shone on their sleeping faces, and a gentle breeze blew in through the open window.
In her dream, Hattie heard a super, super tiny voice coming from Edward's shelf: "I told you there were super-big people living in the garden!"

[P17] The next morning, as Hattie woke up, she saw Edward jumping up and down excitedly. He pulled Hattie to the special shelf. The little cane, hat, slippers, and wings were all gone.
"Look, Hattie! They're all gone! The little people took them away—does that count as evidence?"
"Yes!" Hattie gasped, "I think it might really count."
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《微型拐杖》的封面，展示了森林场景，一个男孩蹲在地上，周围有精灵、小矮人、猫和蘑菇，画面右上角有书名和作者信息。
[P2] 本页为绘本《微型拐杖》的扉页，左侧显示书名和作者信息，右侧绘有一个戴着尖顶帽、手持拐杖、长着翅膀的小精灵站在一片叶子上。
[P3] 本页展示了一幅乡村地图，标注了商店、村庄、学校、通往小树林的路径、高山、游乐场和足球场等地点，画面以绿色山丘和树木为主，呈现宁静的田园风光。
[P4] 哈蒂正在房间里做作业，弟弟爱德华突然冲进来，兴奋地拉着她的外套，声称有重大发现，但哈蒂因专注于算术题而显得不耐烦。
[P5] 爱德华告诉正在做作业的姐姐哈蒂，他觉得花园里可能住着小小人，但哈蒂认为这是无稽之谈，让他自己去玩。
[P6] 爱德华坚持认为花园里有小小人，哈蒂不耐烦地要求他提供证据，最终勉强同意跟他一起去查看。
[P7] 爱德华兴奋地走向花园深处，准备寻找他所说的小小人，画面中可见他沿着石板路前行，旁边有一座小木屋和一只黑猫，树根下还藏着一个戴着尖帽的小精灵。
[P8] 爱德华从花园回来，向姐姐哈蒂展示他找到的‘证据’——一根银白色的微型拐杖，声称是小小人用的，哈蒂对此表示好奇。
[P9] 哈蒂对爱德华带回的‘拐杖’表示怀疑，认为它只是从桦树上掉下的树枝，要求他找到更有说服力的证据；爱德华将‘拐杖’放在自己的架子上后，再次跑进花园继续寻找。
[P10] 爱德华再次从花园回来，向姐姐哈蒂展示他找到的‘证据’——一顶微型帽子，声称是小小人留下的，但哈蒂认为这只是橡子的盖儿，要求他找到更有力的证据。爱德华将帽子放在书架上后，又跑回花园继续寻找。
[P11] 爱德华第三次从花园带回‘证据’——一双毛茸茸的小拖鞋，声称是小小人留下的，但姐姐哈蒂再次否定，认为那是柳絮，并断言世界上没有小小人。
[P12] 爱德华对姐姐哈蒂的怀疑感到失望，他将找到的毛茸茸小拖鞋与之前的小帽子和小拐杖一起放在‘特别架子’上，然后再次前往花园寻找更多证据。
[P13] 爱德华离开后，哈蒂看着他放在架子上的三件‘证据’，笑着摇头，认为他仍相信世界上有小小人，随后继续做作业。
[P14] 爱德华第四次带回‘证据’——一对他认为是小小人翅膀的梧桐树种子，但姐姐哈蒂再次否定，称其为普通种子。爱德华因此感到伤心，开始怀疑世界上是否存在小小人。
[P15] 哈蒂邀请忧郁的爱德华踢足球，爱德华欣然同意，将新找到的‘神仙翅膀’与之前收集的‘证据’放在一起，随后在花园里以5:3的比分赢了姐姐。
[P16] 晚上八点，哈蒂和爱德华上床睡觉，月光透过窗户照进房间。在梦中，哈蒂听到爱德华架子上传来微小的声音，声称花园里住着‘超大人’。
[P17] 第二天早上，爱德华兴奋地发现他收集的小小人‘证据’全部消失，他向姐姐哈蒂展示并询问这是否算作证据，哈蒂最终承认这可能真的算。
